Hon'ble Deepak Verma,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned Aga for the State.

2.  The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the the order dated 04.09.2024 as well as charge sheet dated 04.06.2001 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Varanasi in respect of the Case Crime No.358 of 2000, under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468 I.P.C., Police Station Cantt, District Varanasi, pending in the Court of Pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Varanasi as Criminal Case No.6028 of 2001 (State Versus Lal Chand Singh).
3.

sentences.text:
The discharge application was moved with following prayer:
"That it is crystal 2-clear by perusal of bail register of Sessions Court Varanasi of 2000 that applicant's bail application was grandted on 04.11.2000, It is evident that the applicant was in jail as after grant of bail and after acceptance of bonds got released.
That reason's best known to I.O

While submitting the charge sheet he didn't attach a case diary, statements of witnesses recorded U/S 161 CRPC, site plan and other relevant papers which might have been collected during investigation.
That only the charge sheet and Tehrir had been submitted.
That surprisingly in the absence of all relevant papers the court took cognizance which shows that whicle taking cognizance judicial mind was not applied.
That the office of this court didn't attach bail order, bail bonds and other relevant paper which is a great negligence.
That several other irrelevant papers of any other case are in the file.

That the several letters in this regard as dated: 29.01.2003 and 11.09.2002 were written to I.O. for submitting the relevant papers but all are in vain till today and the police didn't submit the relevant papers.
That the case is for trial not for persecution of the accused.
That there is no evidence against the applicant on record mere Tehrim F.I.R., Charge sheet is not sufficient to frame the charge.
That the presence or absence of the accused is not fruitful in the proceeding of this case in lack of evidence.
That the accused/applicant had moved application earlier but no order has been passed thereupon.

It is therefore prayed that this Honrable court may kindly be pleased to discharge the accused/applicant and justice be done."
4.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. opposed the submission raised by learned counsel for the applicant.

5. Considered the submissions raised by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
From perusal of record, it is apparent that on 04.06.2021 charge-sheet was submitted against the applicant, thereafter, on 03.08.2021 learned Magistrate has taken cognizance in the matter but applicant has not co-operated with the trial and absconded, thereafter, on 26.11.2019 NBW had been issued against the applicant.
Further, on perusal of evidence collected during investigation, prima facie, offence is made out against the applicant.
The order passed by the learned Magistrate is just and proper and no interference is warranted by this Court.
6. The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. lacks merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.

7. However, if the applicant moves a recall application before the concerned court below for recalling the NBW, withing two weeks from today, the court below shall decide his application in accordance with law, expeditiously, preferably within a period of three months from the date of filing of recall application.
8. For the period of two weeks from today or till the time of filing of recall application before the Court below, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against him.
